protocol.promotion_rule: A mechanical pass cannot replace the required blind perceptual review.
protocol.controlled_comparison: Compare prior and updated skills with the same model, brief, grid, palette budget, references, and effort. Shuffle outputs for a non-builder reviewer. Report win/tie/loss/not-assessed per case, and cost separately.

evals.prompt: Create a 16x16 exact-grid lighthouse in a night storm. Compare three anonymous same-grid directions, then finish one selected direction. It must read at native size, use one warm lantern against cool water, and ship as standalone HTML, editable JSON, and PNG.
evals.expected_output: A draft 16x16 lighthouse with three anonymous same-grid directions, explicit silhouette/value checkpoints, a warm focal cue, exact standalone artifacts, and an honest blind-read verdict.
mechanical_assertions: The study contains exactly three materially different 16x16 draft grids and its anonymous payload matches all child grids.
Silhouette, value, and final checkpoints keep exact 16x16 dimensions.
Validation proves JSON, PNG, and HTML parity with no remote URL.
perceptual_questions: Without title or source context, what subject and orientation are visible at 1x?
Which sample has the clearest tower/lantern silhouette and why?
Does cool storm mass stay subordinate to the warm focal cue?
What one signature survives after looking away, and what still reads as generic?

evals.prompt: Recover the supplied full-body character into a transparent 32x32 exact pixel master with at most 16 colors. Preserve the pose and oversized red scarf, remove source noise, and provide editable HTML, JSON, and PNG proof.
evals.expected_output: A transparent authored 32x32 runner draft whose pose and trailing red scarf survive native review, with source provenance, exact parity, and an explicit comparison against automatic conversion.
mechanical_assertions: The original source is targeted directly at 32x32 with contain fit, clean alpha, and at most 16 colors.
The final canonical grid differs from raw automatic conversion and retains explicit source-analysis provenance.
Validation proves JSON, PNG, and HTML parity with no remote URL.
perceptual_questions: Without the prompt, is this a full-body character and what pose is visible?
Does the scarf read as a trailing cloth mass rather than an unrelated red stripe?
Are body, scarf, and background separation clear at native 1x?
Which automatic-source artifacts remain, if any?

evals.prompt: Recover the supplied 32x32 scout-ship fixture into an exact 8x8 master. Compare three anonymous same-grid directions and select one for a single authored repair. Preserve top-down orientation, an amber cockpit cue, and two cool engine cues. Keep the automatic 8x8 baseline and prove that repair without labels.
evals.expected_output: An 8x8 repair case with a preserved losing baseline, three anonymous direction grids, explicit repair decisions, exact proof artifacts, and a blind verdict that may remain draft if craft recognition is ambiguous.
mechanical_assertions: The automatic baseline and authored repair are both exact 8x8 artifacts derived from the versioned 32x32 fixture.
The study contains exactly three materially different 8x8 draft grids.
The repair records non-empty silhouette, identity_cue, and subtraction decisions and preserves the losing baseline.
Validation proves JSON, PNG, and HTML parity with no remote URL.
perceptual_questions: Without title or source, does the final grid read as a top-down craft rather than an abstract badge?
Is the amber cockpit distinct from the hull at native 1x?
Do two engine cues remain separate without turning into noise?
Is the authored repair visibly better than the automatic baseline, or should the verdict remain loss/not-assessed?

evals.prompt: Create an original 32x32 transparent tree for a top-down game with at most eight colors. Compare three anonymous same-grid directions, then finish one selected direction. Use a foliage construction technique and inspect local process references if available. Keep a readable trunk and an asymmetric crown. Show how silhouette, value, and material were built, then repair one observed visual problem.
evals.expected_output: An original draft with reference decisions, part and overlap planning, distinct same-grid directions, buildable passes, and one evidence-based pixel repair.
mechanical_assertions: All masters remain 32x32 with at most eight colors and exact JSON/PNG/HTML parity.
Reference decisions distinguish inspected media, derivative text, and inference; unavailable media are not claimed as viewed.
The patch binds the baseline fingerprint, checks original colors, and preserves every unedited cell.
The source corpus is not copied into the distributable output.
perceptual_questions: Does the tree read at 1x without a title?
Do crown placement and branch overlaps explain the volume before leaf texture?
Are repeated motifs hidden within a coherent crown rather than visible as identical stamps?
Does the repair improve the stated visual problem without damaging the silhouette?

evals.prompt: Create an original 32x32 isometric cargo mech with at most ten colors. Its payload, supported body, feet, and a small optical cue must read at native size. Use a measured projection and an explicit overlap order. Compare three functional silhouettes before finishing the selected machine.
evals.expected_output: A draft machine built from functional parts and consistent screen-space axes, with a native-size anonymous study and honest browser evidence.
mechanical_assertions: The study has three materially different 32x32 draft grids.
Part bounds, anchors, palette roles, and overlap order agree with the declared grid.
The final has at most ten colors and validated JSON/PNG/HTML parity.
perceptual_questions: Is this a cargo-carrying machine rather than a decorated humanoid badge?
Do its feet and support structure plausibly carry the payload?
Do visible faces follow the same projection and light?
Is the optical cue readable without competing with the main form?

evals.prompt: These three original 32x32 drafts are recognizable but may still have important construction problems. Critique each current piece on its own before making a comparison. Choose the two defects with the greatest visible impact, then repair them while preserving the original grid and palette budget: ten colors for the portrait and carrier, seven for the tree. Keep the earlier drafts and report any tradeoff or unresolved read. Do not use an existing after-spec as your answer.
evals.expected_output: A located critique, two independent authored repairs, exact before/after proof, and an honest verdict that separates relative preference from task success.
mechanical_assertions: Each repair remains 32x32 within its declared palette budget and passes exact artifact validation.
The current-only critique precedes access to any bundled after-spec or annotated comparison.
Each intervention names an observed defect, region, causal relationship, operation, and constraint at risk.
Both earlier grids are preserved and no unperformed review is represented as acceptance.
perceptual_questions: Does the critique identify a visible construction or hierarchy failure rather than ask for more detail by default?
Does the repair clarify that failure at native size when compared against the close baseline?
Has a preferred version retained an incorrect functional read or introduced a new tradeoff?
Would the result still seem convincing without a weaker version beside it?
